description: Shared Renovate defaults for the Pinguteca organization.

Non-major updates automerge as soon as checks pass, with no schedule window. Breakage is caught by CI and, for deployed workloads, rolled back by the GitOps controller, so delaying merges to office hours bought latency rather than safety.
Options that merely restate a Renovate default are set explicitly on purpose, so that a default changing upstream shows up as a diff here rather than as silent behaviour drift.
Preset order matters: container-config must precede kubernetes-config so Kubernetes regroups images, and hk-config must stay last so its grouping overrides mise-config for hk dependencies.

Prereleases are skipped, not held. allowedVersions filters them out before an update object exists, so none of them reaches a branch or the Dependency Dashboard. ignoreUnstable stays on as the semantic first pass, and the final rule keeps anything that slips past both off automerge.
prBodyNotes: {{#if isMajor}}:warning: MAJOR UPDATE, may require additional runtime testing to ensure compatibility. :warning:{{/if}}

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes skip the cooldown and are created immediately. automerge is left unset here on purpose. The whole vulnerabilityAlerts object is spread into a packageRule force block, which outranks every other rule, so setting automerge true here merges a major version jump unattended. Left unset, the ordinary update-type rule below decides, so a security patch or minor still merges on its own and a security major waits for a human. dependencyDashboardApproval cannot gate it, because the built-in default forces that to false.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Refresh lock files with no schedule window, the same as every other update here, and merge once checks pass. Renovate defaults this to before 4am on monday, which is the one place a window survived, so it is overridden rather than inherited. Tool and dependency updates already rewrite their own lock files in the same commit, so this only covers the transitive versions no manifest change touches, and running it continuously keeps that gap small instead of sampling it once a week. minimumReleaseAge is cleared on purpose. A lock file maintenance branch moves to no single release, so it carries no releaseTimestamp, and checkUpgradeMinimumReleaseAge applies minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour timestamp-required to it, which marks the branch pending. The renovate/stability-days check then never turns green. The escape hatch next to it, for a package manager that enforces the age itself, cannot help because no manager implements enforcesMinimumReleaseAge yet. Left inherited, the pull request sits with every real check passing and that one stuck, and it never merges. Clearing it removes a gate that was never ageing anything, because the transitive versions a refresh picks up carry no timestamps for Renovate to measure

packageRules.description: Automerge low-risk update types, which cannot be draft PRs because GitHub refuses to merge drafts
Automerge development dependencies, which cannot be draft PRs because GitHub refuses to merge drafts

Hold major development dependency updates. The rule above automerges every update type for devDependencies, which is fine while the change is non-breaking, but a major can break the build or the release pipeline even though nothing reaches consumers. This also catches the security case, where a fix whose lowest remedy is a new major would otherwise merge unattended. draftPR returns to the default so a held major reads like any other major awaiting review, and a security major stays undrafted because vulnerabilityAlerts forces that

Hold a .NET SDK feature band change, and a major with it. dotnet-config gives both the global.json selector and the SDK container image a versioning that treats the feature band as the minor, because stock semver reads 10.0.100 to 10.0.404 as a patch and would merge it unattended, while a band carries a minimum Visual Studio version that Renovate cannot see and has to match the band the rest of the repository asks for. A move inside a band, such as 10.0.401 to 10.0.404, stays a patch and still merges on its own. This rule lives here and not in dotnet-config because a preset's packageRules resolve before the parent's, so the automerge rule above would win over anything the preset set

Skip prereleases outright. ignoreUnstable already keeps a dependency on a stable version from being offered one, but it does nothing for a dependency that already sits on a prerelease: Renovate keeps following that track, and rc.7 to rc.9 classifies as a patch. internalChecksFilter strict compounds it by dropping every release still inside minimumReleaseAge, so the newest eligible version can be a prerelease while the stable one waits out the cooldown. allowedVersions filters candidate releases before any update object is built, so a prerelease produces no branch, no pull request and no Dependency Dashboard entry. The pattern covers the hyphen and dot suffix forms used by semver, NuGet and Maven, and the attached form used by PEP 440. It is anchored at the end, which leaves container variant tags such as alpine, bookworm, musl and devel-ubuntu22.04 alone, along with stable letter releases like openssl 1.1.1a and Go pseudo-versions. The anchor also means a prerelease carrying a trailing variant, such as 1.0.0-rc1-alpine, still gets through, which is the safe direction to fail. It uses no lookaround or backreference, so RE2 and the RegExp fallback agree

Backstop for a prerelease the rule above cannot catch. That pattern reads the version string, so an ecosystem that marks a prerelease some other way slips past it. Renovate also appends its own vulnerability rules after every rule in this file and each one sets allowedVersions to the exact fixed version, so a security fix whose lowest remedy is a prerelease overrides the block and arrives as a pull request. In both cases this keeps it off automerge, restores the draft state and labels it. dependencyDashboardApproval is not used, because Renovate takes that from any one upgrade in a branch and it would stall every unrelated dependency sharing the group, while automerge is taken from every upgrade and so stops the merge alone
